svg.text: Visual proofs with areas, rectangles and volumes
Area of the whole square = sum of its four parts.
The two matching rectangles each have area ab.
The smaller square has side length a − b.
The square’s side is a − b, so its area is (a − b)².
Expanding the product gives a² − 2ab + b².
Difference of two square areas forms a rectangle.
Rearranging the leftover area gives a rectangle
Add the two square expansions: the ±2ab terms cancel.
A cube of side a + b splits into eight smaller blocks.
Think of the side as a + b in all three dimensions.
The signs alternate because the second factor is (a − b).
Sum of cubes: multiply a + b by the quadratic factor.
So only the two cubes remain:
Difference of cubes: multiply a − b by the quadratic factor.
The remainder is the difference of the cubes:
